Nível 2 — Complete o diálogo
docs.text:
A: Good ______! How are you?
B: I'm ______, thanks. And ______?
A: I'm good! ______ to meet you.
B: Nice to meet you ______!

docs.title: Nível 3 — Traduza para o inglês
docs.text:
1. Bom dia! Como você está?
  2. Minha cor favorita é azul.
  3. Eu tenho trinta e dois anos.
  4. Tchau! Tenha um bom dia!
  5. Prazer em conhecê-lo.
  6. Quanto custa? Custa quarenta e cinco dólares.

docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) fifteen, 2) forty-two, 3) eighty, 4) thirty-three, 5) one hundred, 6) sixty-seven, 7) ninety-nine  **Nível 2**: morning (ou afternoon/evening) / fine (ou good/well) / you / Nice / too  **Nível 3**: 1) Good morning! How are you? 2) My favorite color is blue. 3) I am thirty-two years old. 4) Bye! Have a nice day! / Have a good day! 5) Nice to meet you. / Pleased to meet you. 6) How much does it cost? / How much is it? It costs forty-five dollars.

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de descrever sua rotina diária em inglês usando vocabulário essencial de atividades cotidianas e expressões de tempo.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Simple Present
  • Preposições de Lugar e Tempo
  • Vocabulário Básico

docs.title: Atividades da Manhã (Morning Activities)
docs.text:
Inglês Tradução Exemplo wake up acordar I wake up at 6:30 AM. get up levantar-se I get up at 6:45 AM. take a shower tomar banho I take a shower every morning. brush my teeth escovar os dentes I brush my teeth twice a day. get dressed se vestir I get dressed for work. comb/brush my hair pentear o cabelo She brushes her hair. have breakfast tomar café da manhã I have breakfast at 7 AM. make coffee fazer café He makes coffee every morning. leave home sair de casa I leave home at 7:30. go to work/school ir para o trabalho/escola She goes to work by bus.

Wake up vs. Get up: Wake up = abrir os olhos. Get up = sair da cama.

docs.title: Atividades do Dia (Daytime Activities)
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Exemplo arrive at work chegar ao trabalho I arrive at work at 8:30. start work começar a trabalhar I start work at 9 AM. check emails verificar e-mails I check emails first thing. have a meeting ter uma reunião We have a meeting at 10. have lunch almoçar I have lunch at noon. take a break fazer uma pausa Let's take a break. finish work terminar o trabalho I finish work at 6 PM. go home ir para casa I go home by subway.

docs.title: Atividades da Noite (Evening Activities)
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Exemplo arrive home chegar em casa I arrive home at 7 PM. cook dinner cozinhar o jantar She cooks dinner every night. have dinner jantar We have dinner at 8 PM. do the dishes lavar a louça He does the dishes after dinner. watch TV assistir TV I watch TV for an hour. read a book ler um livro She reads a book before bed. study English estudar inglês I study English at night. take a walk dar uma caminhada We take a walk after dinner. go to bed ir para a cama I go to bed at 11 PM. fall asleep adormecer I fall asleep quickly.

docs.title: Atividades do Fim de Semana (Weekend Activities)
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Exemplo sleep in dormir até tarde I sleep in on Saturdays. do the laundry lavar roupa I do the laundry on weekends. clean the house limpar a casa We clean the house on Saturday. go shopping ir às compras She goes shopping on Sunday. go to the gym ir à academia He goes to the gym 3 times a week. hang out with friends sair com amigos I hang out with friends on weekends. play sports praticar esportes They play soccer on Sundays. go to the movies ir ao cinema We go to the movies sometimes.

docs.title: Expressões de Tempo para Rotinas
docs.text: Expressão Tradução Exemplo in the morning de manhã I exercise in the morning. in the afternoon à tarde She studies in the afternoon. in the evening à noite (início) We watch TV in the evening. at night à noite I read at night. every day todo dia I work every day. every week toda semana I clean the house every week. on weekdays nos dias de semana I wake up early on weekdays. on weekends nos fins de semana I sleep in on weekends. once a week uma vez por semana I go to the gym once a week. twice a day duas vezes por dia I brush my teeth twice a day. three times a week três vezes por semana He exercises three times a week.

docs.title: Meios de Transporte
docs.text:
Inglês Tradução by car de carro by bus de ônibus by subway/metro de metrô by train de trem by bike/bicycle de bicicleta on foot a pé by taxi/cab de táxi 
I go to work by bus.        → Eu vou para o trabalho de ônibus.
She walks to school.        → Ela vai a pé para a escola.
He drives to work.          → Ele dirige para o trabalho.

docs.title: Have vs. Take vs. Do vs. Make
docs.text:
Verbo Combinações comuns have breakfast, lunch, dinner, a shower (BrE), a meeting, a break take a shower (AmE), a bath, a nap, a walk, a break do the dishes, the laundry, homework, exercise, housework make breakfast/lunch/dinner (cozinhar), coffee, the bed

Diferença regional: have a shower (BrE) vs. take a shower (AmE) — ambos corretos.

Make vs. Do: Make = criar algo. Do = realizar uma atividade.

docs.title: Telling the Time (Dizendo as horas)
docs.text: Hora Inglês Alternativa 7:00 seven o'clock seven 7:15 seven fifteen (a) quarter past seven 7:30 seven thirty half past seven 7:45 seven forty-five (a) quarter to eight 8:05 eight oh five five past eight 8:50 eight fifty ten to nine 12:00 twelve o'clock / noon midday 00:00 twelve o'clock / midnight —

docs.title: 1. Traduzir "tomar banho" literalmente
docs.text:
• ❌ I take a bath every morning. (bath = banho de banheira)
  • ✅ I take a shower every morning. (shower = chuveiro)

docs.title: 2. Confundir go to bed e go to sleep
docs.text:
• Go to bed = ir para a cama (ação física)
  • Go to sleep / Fall asleep = adormecer (começar a dormir)

docs.title: 3. Usar do quando deveria usar make (e vice-versa)
docs.text:
• ❌ I do dinner. → ✅ I make dinner. (cozinhar)
  • ❌ I make the dishes. → ✅ I do the dishes. (lavar louça)

docs.title: 4. Esquecer the antes de substantivos específicos
docs.text:
• ❌ I do dishes. → ✅ I do the dishes.
  • ❌ I clean house. → ✅ I clean the house.

docs.title: Minha Rotina Diária
docs.text:
I wake up at 6:30 in the morning. I take a shower and brush my teeth.
Then I get dressed and have breakfast. I usually have coffee and toast.

I leave home at 7:30 and go to work by bus. I arrive at work at 8:30.
I start work at 9 AM. I check my emails and have meetings.

I have lunch at noon. I usually eat at a restaurant near the office.
I finish work at 6 PM and go home by bus.

I arrive home at 7 PM. I cook dinner and eat with my family.
After dinner, I do the dishes and watch TV.
I study English for 30 minutes every night.
I go to bed at 11 PM.

On weekends, I sleep in and clean the house. I go to the gym
on Saturday morning and hang out with friends on Sunday.

docs.title: Diálogo — Perguntando sobre rotina
docs.text:
A: What time do you wake up?
B: I usually wake up at 7 AM. What about you?
A: I wake up at 6. I go to the gym before work.
B: Wow! How often do you go to the gym?
A: Three times a week. Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
B: That's great! What time do you finish work?
A: At 5 PM. Then I go home and cook dinner.
B: Do you cook every day?
A: Not every day. Sometimes I order food.

docs.text:

  2. She ______ breakfast at 7 AM.
  3. They ______ the dishes after dinner.
  4. He ______ coffee every day.
  5. We ______ to bed at 11 PM.
  6. I ______ the laundry on Saturdays.

docs.title: Nível 3 — Escreva sua própria rotina em inglês
docs.text: Descreva sua rotina de um dia típico usando pelo menos 10 frases. Inclua: - Horários - Meios de transporte - Atividades da manhã, tarde e noite - Expressões de frequência

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) take, 2) has, 3) do, 4) makes, 5) go, 6) do  **Nível 2**: (5) have lunch, (8) go to bed, (1) wake up, (7) have dinner, (4) go to work, (3) have breakfast, (2) take a shower, (6) arrive home  **Nível 3**: Resposta livre. Verifique se usou Simple Present, expressões de tempo e meios de transporte.

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de participar de conversas simples em situações cotidianas: apresentações, compras, restaurantes, pedindo informações e ao telefone.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Verbo To Be
  • Simple Present
  • Wh- Questions
  • Can e Can't
  • Vocabulário Básico

docs.title: Diálogo Modelo
docs.text:
A: Hi! I'm Maria. What's your name?
B: Hello! My name is Lucas. Nice to meet you.
A: Nice to meet you too! Where are you from?
B: I'm from Brazil, from São Paulo. And you?
A: I'm from Brazil too, from Belo Horizonte.
B: What do you do?
A: I'm a software developer. How about you?
B: I'm a teacher. I teach English.
A: That's great! How long have you been here?
B: About six months.

docs.title: Frases Essenciais
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Uso What's your name? Qual é seu nome? Perguntar o nome Where are you from? De onde você é? Perguntar a origem What do you do? O que você faz? (profissão) Perguntar a profissão How old are you? Quantos anos você tem? Perguntar a idade Do you speak English? Você fala inglês? Sobre idiomas Nice to meet you. Prazer em conhecê-lo. Ao ser apresentado How about you? / And you? E você? Devolver a pergunta

docs.title: Diálogo Modelo
docs.text:
Waiter: Good evening! Welcome! Table for two?
Customer: Yes, please.
Waiter: Right this way. Here's the menu.
Customer: Thank you.

(alguns minutos depois)

Waiter: Are you ready to order?
Customer: Yes. Can I have a steak, please?
Waiter: How would you like it? Rare, medium, or well-done?
Customer: Medium, please.
Waiter: And anything to drink?
Customer: A glass of orange juice, please.
Waiter: Sure. Anything else?
Customer: No, that's all. Thank you.

(após a refeição)

Customer: Can I have the check, please?
Waiter: Of course. Here you go.
Customer: Can I pay by card?
Waiter: Yes, you can.
Customer: Thank you. Keep the change.
Waiter: Thank you! Have a nice evening!

docs.title: Frases Essenciais
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Table for two, please. Mesa para dois, por favor. Can I see the menu? Posso ver o cardápio? I'd like... / Can I have...? Eu gostaria... / Pode me trazer...? What do you recommend? O que você recomenda? Can I have the check/bill? Pode trazer a conta? Can I pay by card/cash? Posso pagar com cartão/dinheiro? Keep the change. Fique com o troco.

docs.title: Diálogo Modelo
docs.text:
Shop assistant: Hi! Can I help you?
Customer: Yes, I'm looking for a T-shirt.
Shop assistant: What size? Small, medium, or large?
Customer: Medium, please. Do you have it in blue?
Shop assistant: Yes, we do. Here you go.
Customer: Can I try it on?
Shop assistant: Of course! The fitting room is over there.

(após experimentar)

Customer: It fits perfectly! How much is it?
Shop assistant: It's $25.
Customer: I'll take it.
Shop assistant: Cash or card?
Customer: Card, please.
Shop assistant: Here's your receipt. Thank you!
Customer: Thank you! Bye!

docs.title: Frases Essenciais
docs.text: Inglês Tradução I'm looking for... Estou procurando... Do you have this in (color/size)? Vocês têm isso em (cor/tamanho)? Can I try it on? Posso experimentar? How much is it? / How much does it cost? Quanto custa? I'll take it. Vou levar. It's too expensive. É muito caro. Do you have anything cheaper? Tem algo mais barato? Where is the fitting room? Onde é o provador? I'm just looking, thanks. Estou só olhando, obrigado.

docs.title: Diálogo Modelo
docs.text:
A: Excuse me, can you help me?
B: Of course!
A: How do I get to the train station?
B: Go straight on this street for two blocks.
   Then turn left at the traffic light.
   The station is on your right, next to the supermarket.
A: Is it far from here?
B: No, it's about a 10-minute walk.
A: Thank you very much!
B: You're welcome!

docs.title: Frases Essenciais
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Excuse me... Com licença... How do I get to...? Como eu chego a...? Where is the...? Onde fica o/a...? Is it far from here? É longe daqui? Go straight. Siga em frente. Turn left / Turn right. Vire à esquerda / Vire à direita. It's on your left/right. Está à sua esquerda/direita. It's on the corner. É na esquina. It's next to / across from... Fica ao lado de / em frente a... It's about 5 minutes by foot. Fica a cerca de 5 minutos a pé.

docs.title: Diálogo Modelo
docs.text:
A: Hello?
B: Hi, this is Maria. Can I speak to Pedro, please?
A: I'm sorry, he's not available right now. Can I take a message?
B: Yes, please tell him to call me back.
A: Sure. What's your phone number?
B: It's 9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1.
A: Got it. I'll let him know.
B: Thank you! Goodbye.
A: Goodbye!

docs.title: Frases Essenciais
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Hello? Alô? This is (name). Aqui é o/a (nome). Can I speak to...? Posso falar com...? He/She is not available. Ele/Ela não está disponível. Can I take a message? Posso anotar um recado? Please call me back. Por favor, me ligue de volta. Hold on, please. / Just a moment. Espere um momento, por favor. Sorry, wrong number. Desculpe, número errado. I'll call back later. Eu ligo de volta mais tarde.

docs.title: 6. Frases de Sobrevivência (Survival Phrases)
docs.text: Inglês Tradução Quando usar I don't understand. Eu não entendo. Quando não compreender Can you repeat that, please? Pode repetir, por favor? Quando não ouvir Can you speak more slowly? Pode falar mais devagar? Quando for rápido demais How do you say _____ in English? Como se diz _____ em inglês? Para aprender palavras What does _____ mean? O que _____ significa? Para pedir definição Sorry, my English is not very good. Desculpe, meu inglês não é muito bom. Para se desculpar Can you write it down? Pode escrever? Quando não entender a pronúncia Where is the bathroom? Onde é o banheiro? Necessidade básica I need help. Eu preciso de ajuda. Emergência How much is this? Quanto custa isso? Compras

docs.title: 1. Usar "I am" para profissão sem artigo
docs.text:
• ❌ I am teacher.
  • ✅ I am a teacher.

docs.title: 2. Dizer "the check" vs. "the bill"
docs.text:
• AmE: Can I have the check?
  • BrE: Can I have the bill?
  • Ambos estão corretos.

docs.title: 3. Confundir this is e I am ao telefone
docs.text:
• ❌ Hello, I am Maria. (ao telefone — soa estranho)
  • ✅ Hello, this is Maria. (correto ao telefone)
  • ✅ Hello, I am Maria. (correto pessoalmente)

docs.title: 4. Traduzir "com licença" como "with license"
docs.text:
• ❌ With license, where is the bathroom?
  • ✅ Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

docs.title: 5. Usar please errado
docs.text:
Please pode ficar no início ou no final: 

✅ Please sit down. / Sit down, please.
✅ Can I have a coffee, please?
❌ Please can I have a coffee? (gramaticalmente OK, mas menos natural)

docs.title: Nível 1 — Associe a situação à frase correta
docs.text: Situação Frase 1. Você quer a conta a. Excuse me, where is the station? 2. Você quer experimentar roupa b. Can I have the check, please? 3. Você está perdido c. This is Maria. Can I speak to Pedro? 4. Você liga para alguém d. Can I try it on? 5. Você não entendeu e. Can you repeat that, please?

docs.title: Nível 2 — Complete o diálogo no restaurante
docs.text:
Waiter: Good evening! Are you ready to ______?
Customer: Yes. ______ I have a pizza, please?
Waiter: Of course. And anything to ______?
Customer: A ______ of water, please.
Waiter: Sure. ______ else?
Customer: No, ______ all. Thank you.

docs.title: Nível 3 — Role-Play: Escreva um diálogo
docs.text:
Escolha uma das situações abaixo e escreva um diálogo de pelo menos 8 linhas:

  1. Você chega a uma loja e quer comprar um par de sapatos.
  2. Você está perdido e pede informações na rua.
  3. Você liga para um amigo e ele não está disponível.

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1-b, 2-d, 3-a, 4-c, 5-e  **Nível 2**: order / Can / drink / glass (ou bottle) / Anything / that's  **Nível 3**: Resposta livre. Verifique se usou as frases essenciais de cada situação e se a estrutura gramatical está correta.

docs.title: Desafio: Grave-se falando!
docs.text:
1. Escolha 2 dos diálogos modelo deste tópico.
  2. Pratique lendo em voz alta até se sentir confortável.
  3. Grave-se falando (pode usar o celular).
  4. Ouça a gravação e compare com a pronúncia de um dicionário online (ex: Cambridge Dictionary).
  5. Repita até melhorar a fluência.

Dica: Não se preocupe com sotaque. O importante é ser compreensível e confiante.

docs.title: Passado Simples — Verbos Regulares (Simple Past — Regular Verbs)
Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de formar e usar o passado simples com verbos regulares em inglês, aplicando corretamente o sufixo -ed e suas regras de ortografia e pronúncia.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Simple Present
  • Pronomes Pessoais

docs.title: Quando usar o Simple Past
docs.text:
O passado simples descreve ações concluídas no passado, com tempo definido:

Uso Exemplo Tradução Ação concluída I worked yesterday. Eu trabalhei ontem. Sequência de eventos She arrived and opened the door. Ela chegou e abriu a porta. Hábitos passados We played soccer every weekend. Nós jogávamos futebol todo fim de semana. Estado passado He lived in London for 3 years. Ele morou em Londres por 3 anos.

docs.title: Formação dos Verbos Regulares
docs.text:
Para verbos regulares, adiciona-se -ed ao verbo base:

Regra Verbo Passado Exemplo Maioria: + -ed work worked I worked yesterday. Termina em -e: + -d live lived She lived in Paris. Consoante + y: y → -ied study studied He studied all night. Vogal + y: + -ed play played They played soccer. CVC (1 sílaba): dobrar + -ed* stop stopped The bus stopped. CVC* (2+ sílabas, tônica final): dobrar prefer preferred She preferred tea. CVC (tônica NÃO final): + -ed* visit visited We visited Rome.

*CVC = Consoante-Vogal-Consoante

docs.title: Forma Afirmativa
docs.text:
Estrutura: Sujeito + verbo-ed + complemento

A forma é igual para todos os sujeitos — sem variação de pessoa:

I worked.        He worked.       She worked.
You worked.      We worked.       They worked.

I watched a movie last night.
She studied English for two hours.
They lived in Brazil for five years.
We visited our grandparents last weekend.

docs.title: Forma Negativa
docs.text:
Estrutura: Sujeito + did not (didn't) + verbo (base) + complemento

Importante: Com didn't, o verbo volta à forma base (sem -ed):

I didn't work yesterday.        (✅ forma base)
I didn't worked yesterday.      (❌ duplo passado)

She didn't study last night.
They didn't watch TV.
We didn't live in São Paulo.

docs.title: Forma Interrogativa
docs.text:
Estrutura: Did + sujeito + verbo (base) + complemento?

Did you work yesterday?         → Você trabalhou ontem?
Did she study English?          → Ela estudou inglês?
Did they visit Rome?            → Eles visitaram Roma?

docs.title: Respostas Curtas
docs.text: Pergunta Sim Não Did you...? Yes, I did. No, I didn't. Did she...? Yes, she did. No, she didn't. Did they...? Yes, they did. No, they didn't.

docs.title: Palavras-chave do Simple Past
docs.text: Expressão Tradução yesterday ontem last night / last week / last month / last year ontem à noite / semana passada / etc. ... ago ... atrás (two days ago, three years ago) in 2020 em 2020 when I was young quando eu era jovem this morning (se já passou) esta manhã

docs.title: As 3 pronúncias do -ed
docs.text:
Esta é uma das maiores dificuldades do passado regular. O -ed tem 3 pronúncias:

Pronúncia Quando Exemplos /t/ Após sons surdos: /p/, /k/, /f/, /s/, /ʃ/, /tʃ/ worked, stopped, watched, washed /d/ Após sons sonoros e vogais played, studyed, lived, called, opened /ɪd/ Após /t/ ou /d/ wanted, needed, started, decided

Regra prática: - Se o verbo termina em som de t ou d → /ɪd/ (sílaba extra) - Se o verbo termina em som surdo → /t/ - Se o verbo termina em som sonoro ou vogal → /d/

docs.title: Exemplos por pronúncia
docs.text:
/t/ /d/ /ɪd/ asked answered wanted cooked called needed finished cleaned started helped enjoyed visited liked lived decided missed loved invited stopped opened painted talked played waited walked rained hated watched studied created

Erro comum de brasileiros: pronunciar -ed sempre como sílaba extra. Diga "wórkt" (worked), não "wór-ked". A sílaba extra só existe quando o verbo termina em /t/ ou /d/.

docs.title: O verbo to be NÃO usa did
docs.text:
O verbo to be tem suas próprias formas de passado:

Presente Passado I am I was You are You were He/She/It is He/She/It was We are We were They are They were 
❌ Did you were tired?
✅ Were you tired?

❌ I didn't was at home.
✅ I wasn't at home.

→ Verbos irregulares serão aprofundados em: Simple Past — Irregular Verbs

docs.title: Simple Past vs. Simple Present
docs.text: Simple Present Simple Past Rotinas atuais Ações concluídas no passado I work every day. I worked yesterday. She studies English. She studied English last year. Do you play soccer? Did you play soccer last weekend?

docs.title: 1. Duplo passado com did
docs.text:
• ❌ Did you watched the movie?
  • ✅ Did you watch the movie?

docs.title: 2. Pronunciar -ed como sílaba extra sempre
docs.text:
• ❌ "I walk-ED to school." (2 sílabas para walked)
  • ✅ "I walkt to school." (/wɔːkt/ — 1 sílaba)

docs.title: 3. Esquecer de usar did na interrogativa/negativa
docs.text:
• ❌ You worked yesterday? (compreensível, mas informal)
  • ✅ Did you work yesterday?

docs.title: 4. Usar did com was/were
docs.text:
• ❌ Did you were happy?
  • ✅ Were you happy?

docs.title: 5. Confundir ortografia com -y
docs.text:
• ❌ He studyed all night.
  • ✅ He studied all night. (consoante + y → ied)
  • ✅ He played soccer. (vogal + y → ed)

docs.title: Diálogo — Fim de semana passado
docs.text:
A: What did you do last weekend?
B: I visited my parents in Campinas. We cooked a big lunch together.
A: That sounds nice! Did you stay the whole weekend?
B: No, I didn't. I returned on Sunday afternoon.
A: What did you do on Sunday evening?
B: I watched a movie and studied a little. And you?
A: I cleaned the house and played video games. Nothing special!

docs.title: Passado Simples — Verbos Irregulares (Simple Past — Irregular Verbs)
Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de identificar e usar os verbos irregulares mais comuns no passado simples, memorizando suas formas e aplicando-os em contextos reais.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text: • Simple Past — Verbos Regulares

docs.title: O que são verbos irregulares?
docs.text:
Verbos irregulares não seguem o padrão de adicionar -ed no passado. Cada verbo tem sua própria forma, que precisa ser memorizada.

A boa notícia: os ~50 verbos irregulares mais comuns cobrem a maior parte do uso cotidiano.

docs.title: Grupo 1 — Base = Past = Past Participle (mesma forma)
docs.text:
Base Past Past Participle Tradução cut cut cut cortar hit hit hit bater/acertar hurt hurt hurt machucar let let let deixar/permitir put put put colocar read* read* read* ler set set set configurar shut shut shut fechar

read: a escrita é igual, mas a pronúncia muda: read /riːd/ (presente) → read /rɛd/ (passado, rima com "red").

docs.title: Grupo 2 — Mudança de vogal

docs.text: Base Past Past Participle Tradução be was/were been ser/estar become became become tornar-se break broke broken quebrar bring brought brought trazer build built built construir buy bought bought comprar catch caught caught pegar/capturar choose chose chosen escolher do did done fazer fall fell fallen cair feel felt felt sentir find found found encontrar forget forgot forgotten esquecer get got got/gotten obter/conseguir have had had ter hear heard heard ouvir hold held held segurar keep kept kept manter leave left left sair/deixar lose lost lost perder make made made fazer/fabricar mean meant meant significar meet met met encontrar/conhecer pay paid paid pagar say said said dizer see saw seen ver sell sold sold vender send sent sent enviar show showed shown mostrar sleep slept slept dormir spend spent spent gastar/passar (tempo) stand stood stood ficar de pé steal stole stolen roubar teach taught taught ensinar tell told told contar/dizer think thought thought pensar throw threw thrown jogar/arremessar understand understood understood entender win won won ganhar/vencer

docs.title: Estrutura (igual ao regular)
docs.text:
Forma Estrutura Exemplo Afirmativa Sujeito + past form I went to the park. Negativa Sujeito + didn't + base I didn't go to the park. Interrogativa Did + sujeito + base? Did you go to the park?

Lembre-se: Na negativa e interrogativa, o verbo volta à forma base (não ao passado): - ✅ Did you go? (forma base) - ❌ Did you went? (passado — ERRADO)

docs.title: 1. Agrupar por padrão sonoro
docs.text: Padrão Verbos -ought/-aught buy→bought, bring→brought, think→thought, teach→taught, catch→caught -ept keep→kept, sleep→slept, sweep→swept -elt/-elt feel→felt, deal→dealt -old/-eld tell→told, sell→sold, hold→held -eft leave→left

docs.title: 2. Verbos que rimam no passado
docs.text:
buy → bought    |  bring → brought   | think → thought
(todos com "ought/aught")

keep → kept     |  sleep → slept     | sweep → swept
(todos com "ept")

say → said      |  pay → paid        | lay → laid
(todos com "aid")

docs.title: 3. Os 10 mais usados (memorize primeiro!)
docs.text:
1. be → was/were
  2. have → had
  3. do → did
  4. go → went
  5. say → said
  6. get → got
  7. make → made
  8. see → saw
  9. take → took
  10. come → came

docs.text: Verbo (Passado) IPA Aproximação Cuidado said /sɛd/ "séd" Não "seide" bought /bɔːt/ "bóot" Não "bauguite" thought /θɔːt/ "thóot" O th é surdo caught /kɔːt/ "cóot" Rima com bought heard /hɜːrd/ "rêrd" Não "ríérd" read (past) /rɛd/ "réd" Rima com red ate /eɪt/ "êit" Rima com eight wore /wɔːr/ "uór" Não "uóri" knew /njuː/ "niú" Não "knêu" wrote /roʊt/ "rôut" Não "uróti"

docs.title: 1. Usar -ed em verbos irregulares
docs.text:
• ❌ I goed to the store. / She buyed a car.
  • ✅ I went to the store. / She bought a car.

docs.title: 2. Usar a forma passada com did
docs.text:

  • ✅ Did you go to the party?
  • ❌ She didn't saw the movie.
  • ✅ She didn't see the movie.

docs.title: 3. Confundir said e told
docs.text:
• say → não precisa de objeto: She said goodbye.
  • tell → precisa de objeto (a quem): She told me goodbye.

docs.title: 4. Pronunciar read (passado) como presente
docs.text:
• Presente: I read books every day. /riːd/ (rima com "need")
  • Passado: I read a book yesterday. /rɛd/ (rima com "red")

docs.title: Diálogo — Viagem
docs.text:
A: Where did you go on vacation?
B: I went to Portugal. I spent two weeks there.
A: That sounds amazing! What did you do?
B: I saw many beautiful places. I ate incredible food and
   I drank amazing wine. I also met some wonderful people.
A: Did you buy any souvenirs?
B: Yes, I bought some tiles and a bottle of port wine.
A: Did you take many photos?
B: Of course! I took hundreds of photos. I can show you later.

docs.title: Narrativa — Um dia difícil
docs.text:
Yesterday was a terrible day. I woke up late because I forgot to set my alarm.
I ran to the bus stop, but the bus had already left. I took a taxi to work,
which cost a lot. When I got to the office, I found out I had a meeting
that I didn't know about. My boss told me about it, but I forgot.
After work, I went to the supermarket and bought some food for dinner.
I made pasta, but I put too much salt. I went to bed early because
I felt exhausted.

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de usar o passado contínuo para descrever ações em progresso no passado, combinar com o passado simples usando when e while, e diferenciar os dois tempos verbais.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Simple Past — Regular
  • Simple Past — Irregular
  • Present Continuous

docs.title: Quando usar o Past Continuous
docs.text: Uso Exemplo Tradução Ação em progresso no passado I was studying at 8 PM. Eu estava estudando às 20h. Contexto/cenário The sun was shining. Birds were singing. O sol estava brilhando. Os pássaros estavam cantando. Ações simultâneas She was cooking while he was cleaning. Ela cozinhava enquanto ele limpava. Ação interrompida I was sleeping when the phone rang. Eu estava dormindo quando o telefone tocou.

docs.title: Formação
docs.text:
Estrutura: Sujeito + was/were + verbo-ing

Sujeito Auxiliar Exemplo I / He / She / It was I was working. You / We / They were They were playing.

docs.title: Forma Afirmativa
docs.text:
I was reading a book at 9 PM.
She was working when I called.
They were watching TV last night.
We were living in London at the time.

docs.title: Forma Negativa
docs.text:
Estrutura: Sujeito + was/were + not + verbo-ing

I wasn't sleeping.           → Eu não estava dormindo.
She wasn't paying attention. → Ela não estava prestando atenção.
They weren't studying.       → Eles não estavam estudando.

docs.title: Forma Interrogativa
docs.text:
Estrutura: Was/Were + sujeito + verbo-ing?

Were you sleeping?           → Você estava dormindo?
Was she working?             → Ela estava trabalhando?
What were they doing?        → O que eles estavam fazendo?

docs.title: When e While — Combinando com Simple Past
When + Simple Past (ação curta que interrompe)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant PC as Past Continuous<br>(ação longa)
    participant SP as Simple Past<br>(ação curta)

    Note over PC: I was sleeping...
    SP->>PC: ...when the phone rang.
    Note over PC: (interrupção)
I was taking a shower when the doorbell rang.
She was driving when it started to rain.
We were having dinner when the lights went out.
They were playing soccer when it began to rain.

Estrutura: Past Continuous + when + Simple Past Ou: When + Simple Past + Past Continuous

When the phone rang, I was sleeping.
= I was sleeping when the phone rang.

docs.title: While + Past Continuous (ações simultâneas)
docs.text:
While I was cooking, she was watching TV.
While he was studying, his brother was playing games.
She arrived while we were having lunch.

Regra prática: - when → normalmente com Simple Past (ação curta) - while → normalmente com Past Continuous (ação longa)

docs.title: Resumo de Combinações
docs.text: Estrutura Significado Exemplo PC + when + SP Ação em progresso interrompida I was reading when he called. While + PC, SP Algo aconteceu durante uma ação While I was walking, I found a wallet. While + PC, PC Ações simultâneas While she was cooking, he was cleaning. SP + while + PC Ação curta durante ação longa He called while I was studying.

docs.title: Simple Past vs. Past Continuous
docs.text:
Simple Past Past Continuous Ação concluída Ação em progresso I read a book yesterday. I was reading a book at 9 PM. She cooked dinner. She was cooking dinner when I arrived. They played soccer. They were playing soccer at that time. 
Yesterday at 8 PM:
- I watched a movie. (terminei de assistir → fato concluído)
- I was watching a movie. (estava assistindo naquele momento → em progresso)

docs.title: 1. Usar was com you/we/they
docs.text:
• ❌ They was playing soccer.
  • ✅ They were playing soccer.

docs.title: 2. Usar Past Continuous para ações concluídas
docs.text:
• ❌ I was watching a movie yesterday. (quando quer dizer "assisti")
  • ✅ I watched a movie yesterday. (ação concluída)
  • ✅ I was watching a movie when she called. (em progresso — correto)

docs.title: 3. Usar Past Continuous para sequência de eventos
docs.text:
• ❌ I was waking up, was taking a shower, and was having breakfast.
  • ✅ I woke up, took a shower, and had breakfast. (sequência → Simple Past)

docs.title: 4. Confundir when e while
docs.text:
• ❌ While the phone rang, I was sleeping. (while + ação curta)
  • ✅ When the phone rang, I was sleeping. (when + ação curta)
  • ✅ While I was sleeping, the phone rang. (while + ação longa)

docs.title: 5. Usar stative verbs no Past Continuous
docs.text:
• ❌ I was knowing the answer.
  • ✅ I knew the answer.

docs.title: Diálogo — O que aconteceu?
docs.text:
A: What were you doing yesterday at 6 PM?
B: I was cooking dinner. Why?
A: Because I called you, but you didn't answer.
B: Oh, sorry! I was listening to music while I was cooking.
   I didn't hear the phone.
A: No problem! What were you making?
B: Pasta. It was delicious!

docs.title: Narrativa — Uma cena descritiva
docs.text:
It was a beautiful Sunday morning. The sun was shining and the birds 
were singing. People were walking in the park. Some children were 
playing near the lake. An old man was sitting on a bench, reading 
a newspaper. A woman was jogging along the path.

Suddenly, a dog ran across the path. The woman was running and didn't 
see it. She tripped and fell. Everyone stopped what they were doing 
and ran to help her.

docs.title: Nível 1 — Complete com was ou were + verbo-ing
docs.text:
1. I ______ (sleep) when you called.
  2. They ______ (play) soccer at 4 PM.
  3. She ______ (cook) dinner.
  4. We ______ (study) together last night.
  5. He ______ (not / work) yesterday.

docs.title: Nível 2 — Combine com when ou while
docs.text:
1. I was taking a shower ______ the phone rang.
  2. ______ she was studying, her brother was watching TV.
  3. He fell asleep ______ he was reading a book.
  4. ______ the teacher came in, the students were talking.
  5. She was walking home ______ it started to rain.

docs.title: Nível 3 — Simple Past ou Past Continuous?
docs.text:
1. I __ (walk) to work when I ____ (see) an accident.
  2. She __ (study) when the lights ____ (go) out.
  3. They ______ (have) dinner at 8 PM yesterday.
  4. While we __ (wait) for the bus, it ____ (start) to rain.
  5. He __ (read) a book when she ____ (arrive).

docs.title: Nível 4 — Traduza para o inglês
docs.text:
1. Eu estava dormindo quando o alarme tocou.
  2. O que você estava fazendo às 10 horas?
  3. Enquanto ela cozinhava, ele lavava a louça.
  4. Estava chovendo quando eu saí de casa.
  5. Eles estavam jogando futebol quando começou a chover.

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) was sleeping, 2) were playing, 3) was cooking, 4) were studying, 5) wasn't working  **Nível 2**: 1) when, 2) While, 3) while, 4) When, 5) when  **Nível 3**: 1) was walking / saw, 2) was studying / went, 3) were having (ou had), 4) were waiting / started, 5) was reading / arrived  **Nível 4**: 1) I was sleeping when the alarm went off. 2) What were you doing at 10 o'clock? 3) While she was cooking, he was doing the dishes. 4) It was raining when I left home. 5) They were playing soccer when it started to rain.

docs.text:

  • British Council — Past Continuous

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de usar will e going to para falar sobre o futuro, entendendo quando usar cada forma e as diferenças entre elas.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Simple Present
  • Present Continuous

docs.title: Duas formas de futuro
docs.text: Forma Uso principal Exemplo will Decisões espontâneas, promessas, previsões I'll help you. going to Planos/intenções, evidências I'm going to study tonight.

docs.title: Formação
docs.text:
Forma Estrutura Afirmativa Sujeito + will + verbo base Negativa Sujeito + will not (won't) + verbo base Interrogativa Will + sujeito + verbo base? 
I will help you.      → I'll help you.
She will not come.    → She won't come.
Will you be there?    → Você estará lá?

docs.title: Quando usar will
docs.text: Uso Exemplo Tradução Decisão espontânea (naquele momento) The phone is ringing. I'll answer it. Vou atender. Promessa I'll always love you. Eu sempre vou te amar. Oferta I'll carry your bags. Eu carrego suas bolsas. Previsão (opinião) I think it will rain. Acho que vai chover. Fato futuro She will be 30 next year. Ela vai fazer 30 ano que vem. Ameaça/Aviso I'll call the police! Vou ligar para a polícia!

docs.title: Formação
docs.text:
Forma Estrutura Afirmativa Sujeito + am/is/are + going to + verbo base Negativa Sujeito + am/is/are + not + going to + verbo base Interrogativa Am/Is/Are + sujeito + going to + verbo base? 
I'm going to study tonight.
She isn't going to come to the party.
Are you going to travel this summer?

docs.title: Quando usar going to
docs.text: Uso Exemplo Tradução Plano/Intenção (já decidido) I'm going to buy a new car. Vou comprar um carro novo. Previsão com evidência Look at those clouds! It's going to rain. Olhe aquelas nuvens! Vai chover. Intenção firme She's going to study medicine. Ela vai estudar medicina.

docs.title: A Grande Diferença: Will vs. Going to
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Q["Você está falando sobre o futuro?"]
    Q -->|"Decisão agora?"| W["Use WILL\n'I'll have the pizza.'"]
    Q -->|"Já planejado?"| G["Use GOING TO\n'I'm going to have pizza tonight.'"]
    Q -->|"Previsão com evidência?"| G2["Use GOING TO\n'It's going to rain.' (nuvens)"]
    Q -->|"Previsão = opinião?"| W2["Use WILL\n'I think it will rain.'"]

docs.title: Comparação lado a lado
docs.text: Situação Will Going to Decisão Espontânea (agora) Planejada (antes) "I'll have the steak." (no restaurante) "I'm going to cook steak tonight." (já planejou) Previsão Baseada em opinião Baseada em evidência "I think Brazil will win." "Brazil is winning 3-0. They're going to win."

docs.title: Contrações
docs.text:
Formal Contração Pronúncia I will I'll /aɪl/ "áiol" you will you'll /juːl/ "iúl" he will he'll /hiːl/ "ríl" she will she'll /ʃiːl/ "xíl" it will it'll /ˈɪtl/ "ítol" we will we'll /wiːl/ "uíl" they will they'll /ðeɪl/ "dêiol" will not won't /woʊnt/ "uôunt" going to gonna* /ˈɡʌnə/ "gâna"

"gonna" é apenas oral/informal. Não use na escrita.

docs.title: Presente Contínuo para futuro
docs.text:
O Present Continuous também pode expressar futuro para planos confirmados com horário/local definido:

I'm meeting John at 5 PM tomorrow. (agenda marcada)
We're flying to Paris next Monday. (passagens compradas)
She's having dinner with her parents tonight. (combinado)

Diferença: going to = intenção. Present Continuous = arranjo confirmado.

docs.title: Shall (formal/BrE)
docs.text:
Shall pode substituir will com I e we para sugestões e ofertas (mais comum no inglês britânico):

Shall I open the window?    → Quer que eu abra a janela?
Shall we go?                → Vamos?
Shall I help you?           → Devo ajudá-lo?

docs.title: 1. Usar will para planos já decididos
docs.text:
• ❌ I will travel to Japan next month. (já comprou passagem)
  • ✅ I'm going to travel to Japan next month.

docs.title: 2. Usar going to para decisões espontâneas
docs.text:
• ❌ (O telefone toca) I'm going to answer it.
  • ✅ I'll answer it. (decisão do momento)

docs.title: 3. Esquecer o to em going to
docs.text:
• ❌ I'm going study tonight.
  • ✅ I'm going to study tonight.

docs.title: 4. Usar will com I think + certeza
docs.text:
• I think it will rain. (opinião — correto com will)
  • Look at those clouds! It's going to rain. (evidência — going to)

docs.title: 5. Duplo futuro
docs.text:
• ❌ I will going to study.
  • ✅ I will study. ou I'm going to study.

docs.title: Diálogo — Planos para o fim de semana
docs.text:
A: What are you going to do this weekend?
B: I'm going to visit my parents on Saturday. And on Sunday,
   I'm going to clean the house.
A: That sounds busy! I don't have any plans yet.
B: Why don't you come with me to my parents' house?
A: That's a great idea! I'll bring some cake.
B: Perfect! They'll love that.

docs.title: Diálogo — Decisões espontâneas
docs.text:
A: I'm hungry.
B: Me too! Let's order food.
A: Good idea. What do you want?
B: I'll have a pizza. What about you?
A: Hmm... I think I'll have sushi.
B: OK, I'll call the restaurant.

docs.title: Nível 1 — Complete com will ou going to
docs.text:
1. (O telefone toca) I ______ answer it!
  2. She ______ study medicine. She already applied to the university.
  3. Look at those clouds! It ______ rain.
  4. I think Brazil ______ win the World Cup.
  5. We ______ move to a new apartment. We already found one.
  6. "There's no milk." — "I ______ buy some."

docs.title: Nível 2 — Complete as frases
docs.text:
1. I ______ (travel) to London next month. I already booked the hotel.
  2. Don't worry. I ______ (help) you with your homework.
  3. She ______ (not / come) to the party. She told me yesterday.
  4. __ you ____ (be) at home tonight?
  5. They ______ (get married) in June. They sent the invitations.
  6. I promise I ______ (not / be) late again.

docs.title: Nível 3 — Traduza para o inglês
docs.text:
1. Eu vou estudar inglês hoje à noite. (já planejado)
  2. Acho que vai chover amanhã. (opinião)
  3. Olhe! O ônibus vai sair! (evidência)
  4. Eu levo suas malas. (oferta espontânea)
  5. O que você vai fazer no sábado? (plano)
  6. Não se preocupe. Eu não vou contar para ninguém. (promessa)

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) 'll (will), 2) is going to, 3) is going to, 4) will, 5) are going to, 6) 'll (will)  **Nível 2**: 1) am going to travel, 2) will help / 'll help, 3) isn't going to come, 4) Will / be, 5) are going to get married, 6) will not be / won't be  **Nível 3**: 1) I'm going to study English tonight. 2) I think it will rain tomorrow. 3) Look! The bus is going to leave! 4) I'll carry your bags. 5) What are you going to do on Saturday? 6) Don't worry. I won't tell anyone.

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de formar e usar comparativos e superlativos para comparar pessoas, lugares, objetos e situações em inglês.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Artigos
  • Simple Present

docs.title: Os três graus do adjetivo
docs.text: Grau Uso Exemplo Normal Descrever She is tall. Comparativo Comparar dois She is taller than me. Superlativo Destacar entre todos She is the tallest in the class.

docs.title: Adjetivos curtos (1 sílaba)
docs.text: Regra Adj. Comparativo Superlativo + -er / -est tall taller the tallest + -er / -est old older the oldest + -er / -est cheap cheaper the cheapest Termina em -e: + -r / -st nice nicer the nicest CVC: dobrar + -er / -est big bigger the biggest CVC: dobrar + -er / -est hot hotter the hottest CVC: dobrar + -er / -est thin thinner the thinnest

docs.title: Adjetivos longos (2+ sílabas)
docs.text: Regra Adj. Comparativo Superlativo more / most expensive more expensive the most expensive more / most beautiful more beautiful the most beautiful more / most interesting more interesting the most interesting more / most comfortable more comfortable the most comfortable

docs.title: Adjetivos de 2 sílabas terminados em -y
docs.text: Regra Adj. Comparativo Superlativo -y → -ier / -iest happy happier the happiest -y → -ier / -iest easy easier the easiest -y → -ier / -iest busy busier the busiest -y → -ier / -iest early earlier the earliest -y → -ier / -iest funny funnier the funniest

docs.title: Adjetivos irregulares
docs.text: Adjetivo Comparativo Superlativo good better the best bad worse the worst far farther/further the farthest/furthest old older/elder the oldest/eldest much/many more the most little less the least

docs.title: Usando Comparativos
docs.text:
Estrutura: Adjetivo comparativo + than

She is taller than her brother.
This book is more interesting than that one.
My car is faster than yours.
English is easier than Chinese.

Than = do que (para comparação)

docs.title: Usando Superlativos
docs.text:
Estrutura: the + adjetivo superlativo (+ in/of)

She is the tallest in the class.
This is the most expensive restaurant in the city.
He is the best student of all.
It's the worst movie I've ever seen.

Use in para lugares/grupos: the tallest in the class Use of para quantidades: the best of all

docs.title: Igualdade: as...as
docs.text:
Estrutura: as + adjetivo (normal) + as

She is as tall as her mother.        → Ela é tão alta quanto a mãe.
This book is as good as that one.    → Este livro é tão bom quanto aquele.
He isn't as fast as his brother.     → Ele não é tão rápido quanto o irmão.

Negativa (not as...as) = "não tão...quanto" (indica que é menos): - He isn't as tall as his brother. = He is shorter.

docs.title: Intensificadores
docs.text: Intensificador Uso Exemplo much / a lot Diferença grande She is much taller than me. a little / slightly Diferença pequena He is slightly older than her. even Comparação enfática This is even better! by far Superlativo enfático She is by far the best.

docs.title: 1. Dupla comparação
docs.text:
• ❌ She is more taller than me.
  • ✅ She is taller than me.
  • ❌ It's the most cheapest option.
  • ✅ It's the cheapest option.

docs.title: 2. Esquecer the no superlativo
docs.text:
• ❌ She is tallest in the class.
  • ✅ She is the tallest in the class.

docs.title: 3. Esquecer than no comparativo
docs.text:
• ❌ He is taller me.
  • ✅ He is taller than me.

docs.title: 4. Usar more com adjetivos curtos
docs.text:
• ❌ She is more tall.
  • ✅ She is taller.

docs.title: 5. Confundir good-better-best e bad-worse-worst
docs.text:
• ❌ She is gooder than me. / The goodest.
  • ✅ She is better than me. / The best.

docs.title: 6. Escrever funnier como funnyer
docs.text:
• ❌ funnyer**
  • ✅ funnier** (y → ier)

docs.title: Diálogo — Comparando cidades
docs.text:
A: Which city do you prefer, São Paulo or Rio?
B: I think Rio is more beautiful than São Paulo.
A: I agree, but São Paulo is bigger and has more job opportunities.
B: That's true. São Paulo is also more expensive.
A: What about Curitiba? Some say it's the best city to live in Brazil.
B: I don't know. I've never been there. But I've heard it's 
   colder than both São Paulo and Rio!
A: Yes, it's the coldest capital in the south.

docs.title: Frases comparativas
docs.text:
My brother is older than me, but I am taller than him.
English is easier than Japanese, but not as easy as Spanish.
This is the best restaurant in town. It's much better than the others.
She is the most intelligent student in our class.
Today is hotter than yesterday. It's the hottest day of the year!

docs.title: Nível 1 — Forme o comparativo e o superlativo
Nível 2 — Complete com a forma correta
docs.text:
1. She is ______ (tall) than her sister.
  2. This is the ______ (good) pizza I've ever had.
  3. My house is ______ (big) than his apartment.
  4. He is the ______ (intelligent) student in the class.
  5. Today is ______ (hot) than yesterday.
  6. This exercise is not as ______ (difficult) as the last one.

docs.title: Nível 3 — Traduza para o inglês
docs.text:
1. Ela é mais alta que eu.
  2. Este é o melhor restaurante da cidade.
  3. Meu irmão é tão inteligente quanto eu.
  4. O inverno é a estação mais fria do ano.
  5. Este livro é mais interessante que aquele.
  6. Ela é a aluna mais aplicada da turma.
  7. Este hotel é muito mais caro que o outro.

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) faster / the fastest, 2) more beautiful / the most beautiful, 3) happier / the happiest, 4) better / the best, 5) bigger / the biggest, 6) more expensive / the most expensive, 7) worse / the worst, 8) easier / the easiest  **Nível 2**: 1) taller, 2) best, 3) bigger, 4) most intelligent, 5) hotter, 6) difficult  **Nível 3**: 1) She is taller than me. 2) This is the best restaurant in the city/town. 3) My brother is as intelligent as me. 4) Winter is the coldest season of the year. 5) This book is more interesting than that one. 6) She is the most dedicated student in the class. 7) This hotel is much more expensive than the other one.

docs.title: Referências
docs.text:
• Cambridge Dictionary — Comparatives and Superlatives
  • British Council — Comparatives and Superlatives
  • Murphy, R. Essential Grammar in Use. Cambridge University Press. Units 87–90.

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de usar os advérbios de frequência corretamente em frases, entendendo sua posição na sentença e a escala de frequência de cada um.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Simple Present
  • Verbo To Be

docs.title: Escala de Frequência
docs.text:
always (100%) ████████████████████ sempre
usually (80%) ████████████████     geralmente
often (60%)   ████████████         frequentemente
sometimes (50%) ██████████         às vezes
rarely (10%)  ██                   raramente
seldom (10%)  ██                   raramente (formal)
never (0%)    ░                    nunca

docs.title: Regra 1: ANTES do verbo principal
docs.text:
I always wake up early.
She usually drinks coffee.
They often go to the gym.
We sometimes eat out.
He rarely watches TV.
I never smoke.

docs.title: Regra 2: DEPOIS do verbo to be
docs.text:
She is always late.           (não: She always is late)
He is usually happy.
They are often busy.
I am sometimes tired.
We are rarely absent.
He is never bored.

docs.title: Regra 3: ENTRE o auxiliar e o verbo principal
docs.text:
I can always help you.
She doesn't usually eat breakfast.
He has never been to Japan.
They don't often go out.

docs.title: Expressões de frequência
docs.text:
Estas expressões geralmente vão no final da frase:

Expressão Tradução Exemplo every day todo dia I exercise every day. every week toda semana She calls me every week. once a week uma vez por semana I go to the gym once a week. twice a month duas vezes por mês We meet twice a month. three times a year três vezes por ano He travels three times a year. on Mondays nas segundas I have class on Mondays. on weekends nos fins de semana We rest on weekends.

docs.title: Sometimes — Posição flexível
docs.text:
Sometimes é o mais flexível — pode ir no início, meio ou fim:

Sometimes I go to the park.     (início)
I sometimes go to the park.     (meio — mais comum)
I go to the park sometimes.     (fim)

docs.title: Never — já é negativo
docs.text:
Never já carrega sentido negativo, então não use don't/doesn't junto:

❌ I don't never smoke.  (dupla negação)
✅ I never smoke.
✅ I don't ever smoke.   (ever = alguma vez, em negativas)

docs.title: Ever — em perguntas e negativas
docs.text: Contexto Uso Exemplo Perguntas ever = alguma vez Do you ever cook? Negativas not...ever = never I don't ever eat fast food. Afirmativas ❌ (não se usa) ❌ I ever cook.

docs.title: Perguntas com How often
docs.text:
How often do you exercise?      → Com que frequência você se exercita?
How often does she travel?      → Com que frequência ela viaja?

Resposta: Use advérbio de frequência ou expressão: - I exercise every day. / I usually exercise three times a week.

docs.title: 1. Posicionar antes do to be
docs.text:
• ❌ She always is happy.
  • ✅ She is always happy.

docs.title: 2. Posicionar depois do verbo principal
docs.text:
• ❌ I drink usually coffee.
  • ✅ I usually drink coffee.

docs.title: 3. Dupla negação com never
docs.text:
• ❌ I don't never eat meat.
  • ✅ I never eat meat. ou I don't ever eat meat.

docs.title: 4. Confundir always com ever
docs.text:
• always = sempre (afirmativa): I always study.
  • ever = alguma vez (pergunta): Do you ever study at night?

docs.title: Diálogo — Hábitos
docs.text:
A: How often do you go to the gym?
B: I usually go three times a week. And you?
A: I rarely go. I'm always too tired after work.
B: You should try going in the morning!
A: I never wake up early enough.
B: I sometimes go at 6 AM. You get used to it!
A: Do you ever go on weekends?
B: Yes, I often go on Saturdays.

docs.title: Nível 1 — Coloque o advérbio na posição correta
docs.text:
1. I am late for work. (never) →
  2. She drinks tea in the morning. (usually) →
  3. They are happy. (always) →
  4. He goes to the cinema. (sometimes) →
  5. We eat fast food. (rarely) →

docs.title: Nível 2 — Traduza para o inglês
docs.text:
1. Eu sempre acordo cedo.
  2. Ela geralmente toma café de manhã.
  3. Eles nunca vão ao cinema.
  4. Nós às vezes jantamos fora.
  5. Com que frequência você estuda inglês?
  6. Ela está sempre atrasada.

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) I am never late for work. 2) She usually drinks tea in the morning. 3) They are always happy. 4) He sometimes goes to the cinema. / Sometimes he goes to the cinema. 5) We rarely eat fast food.  **Nível 2**: 1) I always wake up early. 2) She usually has/drinks coffee in the morning. 3) They never go to the cinema. 4) We sometimes eat out. / We sometimes have dinner out. 5) How often do you study English? 6) She is always late.

docs.title: Referências
docs.text:
• Cambridge Dictionary — Adverbs of Frequency
  • British Council — Frequency Adverbs
  • Murphy, R. Essential Grammar in Use. Cambridge University Press. Unit 96.

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de identificar e usar os pronomes objetos em inglês para substituir substantivos que recebem a ação do verbo ou vêm após preposições.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Pronomes Pessoais
  • Simple Present

docs.title: O que são Object Pronouns?
docs.text:
Os Object Pronouns (pronomes objetos) substituem o objeto de uma frase — a pessoa ou coisa que recebe a ação do verbo ou que vem após uma preposição.

Subject Pronoun (Sujeito - Pratica a ação) Object Pronoun (Objeto - Recebe a ação) I (eu) me (me, mim, comigo) you (você) you (te, você, ti, contigo) he (ele) him (o, lhe, ele) she (ela) her (a, lhe, ela) it (ele/ela - coisas/animais) it (o, a, lhe, ele/ela) we (nós) us (nos, nós, conosco) they (eles/elas) them (os, as, lhes, eles/elas)

docs.title: Sujeito vs. Objeto
docs.text:
A estrutura básica do inglês é: Sujeito + Verbo + Objeto

flowchart LR
    S[Sujeito<br>Subject Pronoun] -->|Pratica a ação| V((Verbo))
    V -->|Recai sobre| O[Objeto<br>Object Pronoun]

    SEx[I] -->|love| OEx[her]
    SEx2[She] -->|loves| OEx2[me]
✅ I love her.       (Eu amo ela / Eu a amo)
❌ I love she.       (ERRADO: "she" só pode ser sujeito)

✅ She loves me.     (Ela me ama)
❌ Her loves me.     (ERRADO: "her" só pode ser objeto)

docs.title: 1. Após verbos (Recebedor da ação)
docs.text:
I see him every day.        → Eu o vejo / vejo ele todos os dias.
Can you help me?            → Você pode me ajudar?
We invited them.            → Nós os convidamos.
He called us.               → Ele nos ligou.
I bought it yesterday.      → Eu comprei isso/ele ontem.

docs.title: 2. Após preposições (with, for, about, to, from, etc.)
docs.text:
This gift is for you.             → Este presente é para você.
I want to go with him.            → Eu quero ir com ele.
Don't talk about them.            → Não fale sobre eles.
Listen to me!                     → Escute-me!
She received a letter from us.    → Ela recebeu uma carta de nós.

docs.title: You e It não mudam
docs.text:
Os pronomes you e it são iguais tanto na forma de sujeito quanto de objeto. A função é determinada pela posição na frase:

You love John. (You = sujeito)
John loves you. (you = objeto)

It is on the table. (It = sujeito)
I bought it yesterday. (it = objeto)

docs.title: Ordem com dois objetos
docs.text:
Quando um verbo tem dois objetos (um direto - "o quê" e um indireto - "para quem"), o pronome objeto geralmente vem logo após o verbo:

Give me the book. (Me dê o livro.)
Show us your photos. (Nos mostre suas fotos.)
He sent her a message. (Ele mandou uma mensagem para ela.)

Se usar to ou for, a ordem inverte: Give the book to me.

docs.title: 1. Usar Subject Pronouns após verbos ou preposições
docs.text:
• ❌ I saw he at the mall.
  • ✅ I saw him at the mall.
  • ❌ This is for she.
  • ✅ This is for her.

docs.title: 2. Confundir his (possessivo) com him (objeto)
docs.text:
• ❌ I love his.
  • ✅ I love him. (O pronome objeto de 'he' é 'him')
  • ✅ I love his dog. (Correto, pois 'his' acompanha o substantivo 'dog')

docs.title: 3. Usar pronomes retos brasileiros ("eu vi ele") traduzidos literalmente
docs.text:
No português falado do Brasil, é comum usar pronomes retos como objeto ("Eu vi ele", "Deixa eu ver"). Em inglês, isso é estritamente incorreto:

  • ❌ I saw he.
  • ✅ I saw him.
  • ❌ Let I see.
  • ✅ Let me see.
  • ❌ Call they.
  • ✅ Call them.

docs.title: Diálogo — Falando sobre amigos e família
docs.text:
A: Did you see Sarah today?
B: Yes, I saw her at the library. I gave her the book she wanted.
A: Great. What about John and Mark?
B: I called them, but they didn't answer. I left a message for them.
A: Okay. By the way, can you help me with this project?
B: Of course! I can help you tomorrow afternoon.

docs.title: Frases comuns
docs.text:
Tell me the truth!                (Diga-me a verdade!)
Let us go!                        (Deixe-nos ir! / Vamos!)
Look at it!                       (Olhe para isso/ele!)
Are you talking to me?            (Você está falando comigo?)
I don't know him.                 (Eu não o conheço.)

docs.title: Nível 1 — Substitua o substantivo em destaque por um pronome objeto
docs.text:
1. I saw Mary yesterday. → I saw ______ yesterday.
  2. We invited Paul and Jane. → We invited ______.
  3. She called Peter. → She called ______.
  4. I bought the car. → I bought ______.
  5. This present is for my mother. → This present is for ______.
  6. Don't look at the children. → Don't look at ______.

docs.title: Nível 2 — Escolha o pronome correto
docs.text:
1. (He / Him) wants to talk to (she / her).
  2. We went to the movies with (they / them).
  3. Do you know (I / me)?
  4. (They / Them) invited (we / us) to the party.
  5. Can you pass the salt to (he / him)?
  6. Look at (it / he)! It's beautiful!

docs.title: Nível 3 — Traduza para o inglês
docs.text:
1. Eu o vi ontem. (ele)
  2. Ela nos ligou na semana passada.
  3. Você pode me ajudar?
  4. Este livro é para ela.
  5. Eu não gosto deles.
  6. Deixe-me ver.

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) her, 2) them, 3) him, 4) it, 5) her, 6) them  **Nível 2**: 1) He / her, 2) them, 3) me, 4) They / us, 5) him, 6) it  **Nível 3**: 1) I saw him yesterday. 2) She called us last week. 3) Can you help me? 4) This book is for her. 5) I don't like them. 6) Let me see.

docs.title: Referências
docs.text:
• Cambridge Dictionary — Pronouns: Personal
  • British Council — Personal Pronouns
  • Murphy, R. Essential Grammar in Use. Cambridge University Press. Unit 59.

docs.title: Quantificadores (Some, Any, Much, Many, A lot of)
Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de usar os quantificadores some, any, much, many e a lot of corretamente, diferenciando seu uso de acordo com o tipo de frase (afirmativa, negativa, interrogativa) e o tipo de substantivo (contável ou incontável).

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Substantivos Contáveis e Incontáveis
  • There Is / There Are

docs.title: 1. Some e Any (Alguns, Algum, Um pouco de)
docs.text:
Usamos some e any quando não sabemos ou não precisamos especificar a quantidade exata. Eles são usados com substantivos plurais e incontáveis.

Palavra Tipo de Frase Principal Exemplo Tradução Some Afirmativa (+) I have some friends. Eu tenho alguns amigos. Any Negativa (-) I don't have any money. Eu não tenho nenhum dinheiro. Any Interrogativa (?) Do you have any questions? Você tem alguma pergunta?

docs.title: Some em perguntas
docs.text:
Usamos some em perguntas quando estamos fazendo um oferecimento ou um pedido (quando esperamos que a resposta seja "sim").

Oferecimento: Would you like some coffee? (Você gostaria de um pouco de café?)
Pedido: Can I have some water, please? (Pode me dar um pouco de água, por favor?)

docs.title: Any em frases afirmativas
docs.text:
Usamos any em frases afirmativas com o sentido de "qualquer":

You can take any book. (Você pode pegar qualquer livro.)
Call me any time. (Ligue-me a qualquer hora.)

docs.title: 2. Much, Many, A lot of (Muito/Muitos)
docs.text:
Estes quantificadores expressam grande quantidade. A escolha depende se o substantivo é contável ou incontável.

Palavra Significado Usado com... Tipo de Frase Exemplo Many Muitos/Muitas Plurais (Contáveis) ?, -, (+) I don't have many friends. Much Muito/Muita Incontáveis ?, - We don't have much time. A lot of Muitos/Muito Ambos Principalmente (+) She has a lot of money.

docs.title: Resumo prático:
docs.text:
1. Frase afirmativa: Use a lot of (serve para tudo!).
  2. Frase negativa ou pergunta com Incontável: Use much.
  3. Frase negativa ou pergunta com Contável (Plural): Use many.
(+) I drink a lot of water. / I have a lot of friends.
(-) I don't drink much water. / I don't have many friends.
(?) Do you drink much water? / Do you have many friends?

docs.title: 3. How much e How many (Quanto/Quantos?)
docs.text:
Usados para perguntar a quantidade.

Palavra Usado com... Significado Exemplo How many Plurais (Contáveis) Quantos/Quantas? How many brothers do you have? How much Incontáveis Quanto/Quanta? How much time do we have? How much Perguntar o preço Quanto custa? How much is this shirt?

docs.title: A few e A little (Poucos/Pouco)
docs.text:
Para quantidades pequenas, usamos a few e a little:

Palavra Significado Usado com... Exemplo A few Alguns/Poucos Plurais (Contáveis) I have a few friends in London. A little Um pouco de Incontáveis I speak a little French.

Se tirarmos o artigo a, o sentido muda de algo neutro/positivo para algo negativo (insuficiente): - I have a few friends. (Tenho alguns amigos = bom) - I have few friends. (Tenho poucos amigos = ruim/solitário) - I have a little time. (Tenho um pouco de tempo = dá para fazer algo) - I have little time. (Tenho pouco tempo = insuficiente/estou apressado)

docs.title: 1. Usar some em frases negativas
docs.text:
• ❌ I don't have some money.
  • ✅ I don't have any money.

docs.title: 2. Usar much e many trocados
docs.text:
Lembre-se: much = incontável (singular), many = contável (plural com 's').

  • ❌ How much cars are there?
  • ✅ How many cars are there?
  • ❌ I don't have many money. (Dinheiro é incontável!)
  • ✅ I don't have much money.

docs.title: 3. Usar much em frases afirmativas (soa artificial)
docs.text:
• ❌ I have much money. (Gramaticalmente OK, mas muito formal/estranho)
  • ✅ I have a lot of money. (Natural e recomendado)

docs.title: Diálogo — Preparando um jantar
docs.text:
A: Do we have any eggs in the fridge?
B: Let me check. Yes, we have some eggs, but we don't have any milk.
A: How much milk do we need?
B: Just a little. A bottle is fine. 
A: Okay. And do we have many tomatoes?
B: No, we only have a few. We should buy a lot of tomatoes for the sauce.
A: Got it. I'll go to the supermarket. Do you need any help?
B: No, thanks. I can handle the rest.

docs.title: Frases Úteis
docs.text:
There is some water in the glass.
Are there any apples left?
Would you like some tea?
I have a lot of work to do today.
How many people are coming to the party?
How much time did you spend on this?
I only have a little money.

docs.title: Nível 1 — Escolha entre some e any
docs.text:
1. I need ______ sugar for the cake.
  2. Do you have ______ brothers or sisters?
  3. We don't have ______ time left.
  4. Would you like ______ coffee?
  5. I bought ______ apples yesterday.

docs.title: Nível 2 — Escolha entre much, many ou a lot of
docs.text:
1. How ______ milk is in the fridge?
  2. I don't read ______ books.
  3. She has ______ friends in New York. (+)
  4. How ______ cars are in the parking lot?
  5. We don't have ______ money for the trip.

docs.title: Nível 3 — Traduza para o inglês
docs.text:
1. Eu tenho alguns amigos.
  2. Eu não tenho nenhum dinheiro.
  3. Quantos carros você tem?
  4. Quanto tempo nós temos?
  5. Ela toma muita água. (afirmativa)
  6. Você gostaria de um pouco de chá?

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) some, 2) any, 3) any, 4) some (oferecimento), 5) some  **Nível 2**: 1) much, 2) many, 3) a lot of, 4) many, 5) much  **Nível 3**: 1) I have some friends. 2) I don't have any money. 3) How many cars do you have? 4) How much time do we have? 5) She drinks a lot of water. 6) Would you like some tea?

docs.title: Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de usar preposições de movimento para descrever direção, rotas e trajetórias de pessoas e objetos em inglês.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Preposições de Lugar e Tempo
  • Imperativo

docs.title: Conceitos Fundamentais
docs.text: Diferente das preposições de lugar (que mostram onde algo está estacionário), as preposições de movimento mostram a direção para onde algo vai. Elas são frequentemente usadas com verbos de movimento (go, walk, run, drive, fly, jump).

docs.title: As Principais Preposições de Movimento
docs.text: Preposição Significado / Uso Exemplo Tradução to para (direção/destino) She is going to the store. Ela está indo para a loja. into para dentro de He walked into the room. Ele entrou na sala. out of para fora de They ran out of the building. Eles correram para fora do prédio. towards em direção a Walk towards the light. Caminhe em direção à luz. away from para longe de The dog ran away from me. O cachorro correu para longe de mim. across através de / cruzar (superfície) We walked across the bridge. Nós atravessamos a ponte. through através de (volume/túnel) The train went through the tunnel. O trem passou pelo túnel. over por cima de The cat jumped over the wall. O gato pulou por cima do muro. under por baixo de The boat sailed under the bridge. O barco navegou por baixo da ponte. past passar por Drive past the hospital. Passe pelo hospital. up para cima (subir) He ran up the stairs. Ele subiu as escadas correndo. down para baixo (descer) She walked down the street. Ela desceu a rua. along ao longo de We walked along the beach. Nós caminhamos ao longo da praia. around ao redor de They walked around the lake. Eles caminharam ao redor do lago.

docs.title: To vs. Towards
docs.text:
• To: O foco é o destino final. (I'm going to London. = Londres é meu destino)
  • Towards: O foco é a direção, não necessariamente o destino. (He is walking towards me. = Ele está vindo na minha direção)

docs.title: Across vs. Through
docs.text:
• Across: Atravessar uma superfície plana (rua, rio, ponte, campo). Movimento de um lado a outro. (Walk across the street.)
  • Through: Atravessar um espaço tridimensional (túnel, floresta, porta, janela, multidão). (Drive through the forest.)

docs.title: Into vs. In
docs.text:
• Into: Indica movimento do exterior para o interior. (She walked into the house.)
  • In: Indica posição estática no interior. (She is in the house.)

docs.title: Verbos compostos (Phrasal Verbs) comuns de movimento
docs.text:
Muitas dessas preposições formam verbos importantes quando combinadas com get:

Verbo Uso get into entrar (em carro, táxi) get out of sair (de carro, táxi, prédio) get on embarcar (ônibus, trem, avião, navio, bicicleta) get off desembarcar (ônibus, trem, avião, navio, bicicleta) 
I got into the car. (Entrei no carro.)
He got off the bus. (Ele desceu do ônibus.)

docs.title: A exceção Home
docs.text:
A palavra home não aceita a preposição to quando usada com verbos de movimento:

  • ❌ I'm going to home.
  • ✅ I'm going home.
  • ❌ She walked to home.
  • ✅ She walked home.

Com house, a preposição é necessária: I'm going to my house.

docs.title: 1. Usar to com home
docs.text:
• ❌ I went to home.
  • ✅ I went home.

docs.title: 2. Confundir across e through
docs.text:
• ❌ We drove across the tunnel. (O túnel é 3D)
  • ✅ We drove through the tunnel.
  • ❌ She walked through the road. (A estrada é plana)
  • ✅ She walked across the road.

docs.title: 3. Usar in em vez de into para movimento
docs.text:
• ❌ He jumped in the pool. (Gramaticalmente aceito coloquialmente, mas menos preciso)
  • ✅ He jumped into the pool. (Mostra o movimento de fora para dentro)

docs.title: 4. Entrar e sair de transporte
docs.text:
• ❌ Get in the bus. / Get out of the bus.
  • ✅ Get on the bus. / Get off the bus.
  • ❌ Get on the car.
  • ✅ Get into the car.

docs.title: Diálogo — Direções detalhadas
docs.text:
A: Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?
B: It's easy. Walk along this street, go past the supermarket, and turn left.
A: Okay. Past the supermarket and turn left.
B: Yes. Then walk across the park and go over the small bridge.
   The museum is right in front of you. You can't miss it!
A: Thank you so much!

docs.title: Narrativa — Um passeio acidentado
docs.text:
The dog ran out of the house and jumped over the fence. 
It ran across the street and went into the park. 
I ran after it, past the big trees and around the lake. 
Finally, it ran through the bushes and sat under a bench.

docs.title: Nível 1 — Escolha a preposição correta
docs.text:
1. The train went ______ (through / across) the tunnel.
  2. She jumped ______ (in / into) the swimming pool.
  3. They walked ______ (along / past) the river for an hour.
  4. Go ______ (past / through) the bank and turn right.
  5. The cat climbed ______ (up / over) the tree.
  6. He took a plane ______ (to / towards) Paris.

docs.title: Nível 2 — Complete com a preposição de movimento
docs.text:
Use: into, out of, across, over, under, towards

  1. The boy kicked the ball ______ the wall. (por cima)
  2. We had to walk ______ the street to get to the store. (atravessar)
  3. Take your hands ______ your pockets! (para fora de)
  4. The car was driving ______ me very fast! (em direção a)
  5. The dog crawled ______ the bed to hide. (por baixo)
  6. Please, come ______ the house. It's cold outside! (para dentro)

docs.title: Nível 3 — Corrija os erros (se houver)
docs.text:
1. I am going to home now.
  2. Get in the train, it's leaving!
  3. We walked through the bridge.
  4. She ran out of the room crying.

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) through, 2) into, 3) along, 4) past, 5) up, 6) to  **Nível 2**: 1) over, 2) across, 3) out of, 4) towards, 5) under, 6) into  **Nível 3**:  1) I am going **home** now. (Sem 'to') 2) Get **on** the train... (Transporte onde se pode ficar de pé) 3) We walked **across** the bridge. (Superfície) 4) Correto.

docs.title: Palavras de Ligação (Linking Words: and, but, because, so)
Objetivo
docs.text: Ao final deste tópico, o estudante será capaz de conectar ideias simples usando as palavras de ligação and, but, because e so, tornando suas frases mais complexas e fluidas.

docs.title: Pré-requisitos
docs.text:
• Simple Present
  • Simple Past

docs.title: O que são Linking Words?
docs.text:
Palavras de ligação (conjunções) são usadas para unir duas frases ou ideias, mostrando a relação entre elas. Isso evita que falemos em frases curtas e "picotadas".

Palavra Função Significado and Adição / Informação extra e but Contraste / Oposição mas, porém because Razão / Motivo porque (resposta) so Resultado / Consequência então, por isso

docs.title: 1. And (Adição)
docs.text:
Usado para unir ideias semelhantes, adicionar informações ou listar itens.

I like coffee. I like tea.
→ I like coffee and tea.

He woke up. He took a shower.
→ He woke up and took a shower.

She speaks English, Spanish, and French.

Dica de pontuação: Em inglês, costuma-se usar vírgula antes do and no final de uma lista com 3 ou mais itens (conhecida como Oxford comma): red, blue, and green.

docs.title: 2. But (Contraste)
docs.text:
Usado para unir duas ideias opostas, surpreendentes ou contrastantes. Geralmente vem precedido por vírgula ao unir duas frases completas.

I like coffee. I don't like tea.
→ I like coffee, but I don't like tea.

The shoes are beautiful. They are very expensive.
→ The shoes are beautiful, but they are very expensive.

He studied a lot, but he failed the test.

docs.title: 3. Because (Motivo/Razão)
docs.text:
Usado para dar o motivo ou a justificativa de algo. Responde à pergunta Why? (Por quê?).

Why are you tired?
→ I am tired because I worked all day.

She didn't go to work because she was sick.
I am studying English because I want to travel.

Atenção: Because também pode iniciar a frase, embora seja menos comum na fala do dia a dia: Because she was sick, she didn't go to work.

docs.title: 4. So (Resultado/Consequência)
docs.text:
Usado para mostrar o resultado ou a consequência de uma ação. É o oposto de because.

I worked all day. I am tired.
→ I worked all day, so I am tired.

She was sick, so she didn't go to work.
It was raining, so we stayed at home.

Comparação Because vs. So: - Motivo + SO + Resultado - Resultado + BECAUSE + Motivo

I was hungry, so I ate an apple. (Tive fome, então comi uma maçã.) I ate an apple because I was hungry. (Comi uma maçã porque tive fome.)

docs.title: Because vs. Why
docs.text:
Em inglês, existem duas palavras para "por que":

  • Why: Usado em perguntas ("por que").
  • Because: Usado em respostas e justificativas ("porque").
❌ Because are you sad?
✅ Why are you sad?

❌ I'm sad why it's raining.
✅ I'm sad because it's raining.

Informalmente, falantes nativos frequentemente abreviam because para 'cause ou cuz na fala e mensagens de texto: "I'm tired 'cause I worked late."

docs.title: Outras palavras de ligação do nível A2
docs.text: Palavra Significado Exemplo or ou (alternativa) Do you want tea or coffee? although embora (contraste) Although it was raining, we went out. however no entanto (contraste) It was expensive. However, I bought it.

docs.title: 1. Confundir So com Very
docs.text:
No português, às vezes dizemos "Ele é tão legal" para dizer "muito legal". Em inglês, so como conectivo significa "então/por isso". (So também significa "tão", mas preste atenção na estrutura).

  • It was cold, so I wore a jacket. (Conectivo: então)
  • It was so cold. (Intensificador: tão/muito)

docs.title: 2. Usar vírgula errada com because
docs.text:
Geralmente, não se usa vírgula antes de because no meio da frase.

  • ❌ I stayed home, because it was raining.
  • ✅ I stayed home because it was raining.

docs.title: 3. Usar because e so na mesma frase
docs.text:
É redundante usar ambos para a mesma relação de causa e efeito.

  • ❌ Because I was tired, so I went to bed. (Use um ou outro)
  • ✅ Because I was tired, I went to bed.
  • ✅ I was tired, so I went to bed.

docs.title: Diálogo — Contando sobre o fim de semana
docs.text:
A: How was your weekend?
B: It was good, but very busy! I woke up early on Saturday
   because I had to study.
A: Did you study all day?
B: No, I studied in the morning, and then I met some friends.
   We wanted to play soccer, but it started to rain.
A: Oh, what a pity! What did you do?
B: It was raining, so we went to the cinema instead.
   We watched a comedy because we wanted to relax.

docs.title: Narrativa Simples
docs.text:
Yesterday, I went to the supermarket because I needed to buy food.
I bought bread, milk, eggs, and fruit. I wanted to buy fish, but 
it was too expensive, so I bought chicken instead.

docs.title: Nível 1 — Escolha a palavra correta (and, but, because, so)
docs.text:
1. I am hungry, ______ I don't have any money.
  2. I studied hard, ______ I passed the exam.
  3. She didn't buy the dress ______ it was too small.
  4. I like playing tennis ______ watching movies.
  5. He went to the doctor ______ he was feeling sick.

docs.title: Nível 2 — Una as frases usando a palavra indicada
docs.text:
1. It was raining. We stayed at home. (so)
  2. I like dogs. I don't like cats. (but)
  3. She went to bed. She was tired. (because)
  4. I bought a shirt. I bought a pair of shoes. (and)

docs.title: Nível 3 — Traduza para o inglês usando and, but, because, so
docs.text:
1. Eu gosto de maçãs, mas eu não gosto de laranjas.
  2. Ele não foi trabalhar porque estava doente.
  3. Estava frio, então eu fechei a janela.
  4. Eu levantei, tomei banho e tomei café da manhã.
  5. Por que você está feliz? Porque hoje é sexta-feira!

docs.title: Gabarito
docs.text: Clique para ver as respostas  **Nível 1**: 1) but, 2) so, 3) because, 4) and, 5) because  **Nível 2**: 1) It was raining, so we stayed at home. 2) I like dogs, but I don't like cats. 3) She went to bed because she was tired. 4) I bought a shirt and a pair of shoes.  **Nível 3**: 1) I like apples, but I don't like oranges. 2) He didn't go to work because he was sick. 3) It was cold, so I closed the window. 4) I got up, took a shower and had breakfast. 5) Why are you happy? Because today is Friday!

  • British Council — Conjunctions
